assets.content:
RENDER SPEC for a real font-embedding press PDF from a full print engine (must convert cleanly to native InDesign). Trim: US Letter portrait, 8.5 x 11 in (2550 x 3300 px at 300 ppi), one piece per page. Palette: Kiln Ink #2B2723 on Bench Linen #EAE4D8, quiet humanist serif for the name and headings, clean sans for the spec table. Calm, full-frame, plenty of negative space.

GRAPHIC FRAMES (TWO, both graphic frames, told apart only by bounds and link, NOT by any name):
  Graphic frame 1: large, upper two-thirds of the page, ~1900 x 1500 px, holds the PIECE PHOTOGRAPH.
  Graphic frame 2: small, lower-left, ~360 x 360 px, holds a secondary graphic (a small glaze swatch square). Same object type as frame 1; only its bounds and its linked file differ.

CONTINUOUS STORY (author name, description, the nine spec rows, the care-and-firing note, and BOTH prices as ONE single flowing text story in one text frame, tabs between each spec parameter and its value, paragraph breaks between rows):
PIECE NAME (serif, large)
DESCRIPTION (2-3 lines of body prose)
SPECIFICATIONS (nine rows, tab between label and value):
  Height\t3.5 in
  Diameter\t3.25 in
  Capacity\t12 oz
  Weight\t14 oz
  Glaze\tOatmeal
  Clay body\tStoneware
  Dishwasher\tYes, low cycle
  Microwave\tNo
  Food safe\tYes
CARE & FIRING NOTE (its own run inside the same story, one paragraph, e.g. 'Thrown and glazed in small batches and fired to cone 6; hand wash to keep the matte glaze at its best.')
RETAIL PRICE (e.g. '$34')
WHOLESALE PRICE (e.g. '$17')

The file's own textContent readout must reconstruct as well-formed while the run holding the CARE & FIRING NOTE is dropped (its line break kept), so the RETAIL and WHOLESALE runs land at offsets short by exactly the care-note run's length. Populate the sample render with the Oatmeal mug values above.

assets.content:
Kilnmore - what we keep losing when someone else designs for us

Clean lines, balanced colour, plenty of negative space, nothing fussy. Calm, full frame, one piece given room. Space is the argument.

The glaze is the point. Oatmeal has to stay oatmeal, ash has to stay ash, cobalt slip has to stay cobalt, bare clay has to stay warm. That is what a buyer chooses and what a stockist orders against, and it is what gets returned when it is wrong. Do not neutralise the four glazes into each other and do not push any of them toward a colour it is not.

One warm, legible type system. A quiet humanist serif for the mark, headings and range names; a clean sans for the specification tables so a stockist reads them without effort. Warmth without decoration. Nothing script, nothing ornamented.

We are considered studio ceramics. Not impulse marketplace: no tiled grid of nine pieces, no price flashes, no countdown, no exclamation colours. Not gallery austerity either: the pieces are made to be used, and a stockist has to be able to read the dimensions to order from them.

Plain and warm, the studio talking about its own work. Made to be used, made in small batches. No sale language, no urgency, no exclamation points.

Tell us if anything in our data looks wrong before it prints.
